title: BATS bottle records show a 10.8 umol/kg oxygen loss on the 26.5 density surface between 1989-1998 and 2016-2025
abstract: We tested whether vertical motion of water layers can explain long-term oxygen change at the Bermuda Atlantic Time-series Study site. We used BCO-DMO bottle data version 10, quality flag 2, and samples within 50 km of the site. We compared 1989-1998 with 2016-2025 with equal calendar-month weights and a three-year block bootstrap. On potential density anomaly 26.5 kg/m3, oxygen fell from 197.88 to 187.12 umol/kg. The change was -10.76 umol/kg, with an approximate 95% interval of -12.42 to -9.20. Equilibrium oxygen increased by 0.62 umol/kg. Apparent oxygen utilization increased by 11.38 umol/kg. The oxygen loss remained with 1994-2003 as the early period (-8.75) and after a paired comparison with 2000 m oxygen (-9.34 for the main periods). Oxygen near 300 m fell by 3.73 umol/kg against 1989-1998, but its change against 1994-2003 was uncertain. A stricter density interpolation rule left incomplete seasonal coverage and gave no valid contrast. Nitrate plus nitrite increased in the main density selection. Under the main sampling rules, an unchanged oxygen-density profile with vertical motion alone cannot explain the fixed-density loss. One site, wide interpolation brackets, missing samples, possible measurement errors and short period windows limit this result. It does not identify ventilation or respiration as the cause. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, simulation draws and figures are included. Source records remain external.

display.caption: BATS oxygen and water-layer depth in 1989-2025. Annual plot values have a calendar-month adjustment. Shading marks the two comparison periods. Panel C shows equal-month period changes and approximate 95% three-year block bootstrap intervals. Oxygen fell on density 26.5 while oxygen solubility increased. Source: BATS and BCO-DMO dataset 3782 version 10. Calculations and figure are new.

Oxygen changes from 1989-1998 to 2016-2025 across depth and density targets, and checks on the 26.5 density comparison. The later early period retains an oxygen loss. Strict density brackets remove too many calendar months to give a valid equal-month contrast. Adjacent density targets have weaker coverage. Bars show approximate 95% three-year block bootstrap intervals. Source: BATS and BCO-DMO dataset 3782 version 10.
